Confirmed via fnasm.py that the surrounding region is opcode-identical to target (only register color differs) -- the `s32 alpha = e->alpha;` local matches target exactly. do_enemies is therefore at its structural ceiling for THIS law; its one remaining residual is a different, already-documented lever. sfx.c::ProcessEffects::damagetype (e->damagetype at line 2904, inside the SAME function whose `flags` field was fixed by the law-originating session, a distinct site never touched by that fix): full asm trace via fnasm.py+grep for the `,180(` (offsetof(Effect,damagetype)=0xb4=180) pattern found target ITSELF caches damagetype in r22 across the `for(j=0;j<4;j++)` player-hit loop (loaded once at target offset 0x988 before the loop, masked with the DMG_NOHITFX bits at 0x994-0x99c exactly matching source line 2907's `(damagetype & ~0x170) | DMG_NOHITFX`, then reused unchanged via `mr r5,r22` at 0xae4 for the damage_player() call INSIDE the loop, spanning NormalVector2D/fn_8005FB48/damage_player calls with no reload) -- i.e. target explicitly does NOT reread this field across the loop's calls, confirming the C source's cache is the semantically-required exception the law itself carves out (comparing/using a locally-modified value, not the raw field). Separately, target DOES fresh-reload e->damagetype via a distinct `lwz r0,180(r31)` at 0xb38 (right after the damage_player call) for the DIFFERENT `e->damagetype & 0x800` check at source line 2961 -- our source already expresses that as a separate raw `e->damagetype` read, matching. Both sub-patterns confirmed byte-correct; damagetype is innocent.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.scalar-field-cache-defeats-call-boundary-reload.20260830.v1: the law under test -- screened directly against 34 regex-matched candidates across 9 files (enemy.c x23, combat.c x1, mb_particle.c x3, pb_objregs.c x1, psfx.c x1, sfx.c x1, gutil.c x1, options.c x1, camera.c x1, worldcol.c x1); none confirmed a defeat. claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast/multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing/offsetof-*: screened as adjacent alias-form families, not directly applicable (none of the confirmed-innocent sites involved a typed-alias or offsetof conversion). claim.law.large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression: not applicable, zero edits were made so there is no batch to bisect.
attributes.methodology: 1) `python tools/gdl/lowmatch.py --min 50 --max 99 --min-size 150 --sort impact` for the NonMatching queue, cross-referenced against the 8 sibling-claimed TUs (excluded) and the extern-conflict claim (body edits still open). 2) A python regex scanner (single-field `TYPE var = ptr->field;` declaration, 2+ later bare uses of var, a call passing ptr interleaved between first and last use) over src/game excluding the 8 claimed files -- 34 hits. 3) For each hit, resolved the enclosing function and its report.json fuzzy score; any hit inside an already-100.00%-matched function was dropped immediately (17 of 34: move_logic00/06/08x2/14/16/20/29/30/31, getNewDirConeShare, getNewDirFrame, camera_run_mode, WorldObjCollide, StartMissile, and the whole gutil.c TU) as trivially innocent -- editing a matched function for zero gain is prohibited by the monotonic-result policy regardless of pattern match. 4) For the remaining 17 hits in genuinely NonMatching functions, ran `fndiff --ops` on the enclosing function and checked whether any STRUCTURAL opcode-mismatch cluster's byte offset falls inside the candidate's use/call span; only clusters overlapping the candidate were investigated further with `fnasm.py` on both target and ours at that offset. do_enemies (the anchor) and ProcessEffects's new `damagetype` site (a second, previously-unconverted local in the SAME function the law was discovered in) got full manual asm reads since they were the highest-value candidates.
attributes.related_bug_out_of_scope: do_enemy_move (game/enemy/enemy.c) has a CONFIRMED but differently-shaped structural bug, found while screening alg/rad/hht: at the 'hit a player' block (source lines 686-692, alg in {7,8,10,20}), `*(u32*)((u8*)e->coll_ip + 100)` is read at line 687 and `(f32*)((u8*)e->coll_ip + 52)` is read again at line 690 with NO intervening call or store -- straight-line C. Target re-issues a genuine second `lwz r3,652(r30)` (offsetof(Enemy,coll_ip)=0x28c=652, struct-verified) at target offset 0x9c4, but our compiled object CSEs the two syntactically-separate raw dereferences into one load and reuses the register (fndiff --ops: `delete T[625:626]@9c4-9c8=['lwz'] O[625:625]@9c4=[]`, i.e. target has an lwz we're missing). This does NOT match claim.law.scalar-field-cache-defeats-call-boundary-reload's precondition (no named local variable is caching the field, and there is no intervening function call to invalidate aliasing) -- it is address-CSE across two textually-repeated raw dereferences with no call boundary, closer to the project's existing cast-transit/repeated-cast law family (claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast is about the OPPOSITE direction: repeated casts REGRESSING a matched fn by preventing CSE, not this case where CSE happens and shouldn't). No known law in the corpus covers 'target re-reads a raw pointer dereference MWCC provably CSEs safely with no call between them' and no portable-C counter-form was found in the time available (forcing a fresh read of unmodified memory with no intervening call/write is not something standard C semantics let you express without an artificial trick, which the mandatory result policy prohibits) -- left unconverted, function unchanged, flagged here for a future session with a different law hypothesis (possibly: the true original source held an intermediate local for the +100 check whose reload came from register-pressure spill rather than a repeated raw dereference, which is a distinct, not-yet-formulated law).
